dock.behavior.fixed.desc: Reserves screen space, so maximized apps stop above the dock. Choose Smart to use the full screen.
dock.behavior.smart.desc: Hides when a window overlaps it. Maximized apps can use the full screen.
dock.behavior.peek.desc: Stays hidden until you move the pointer to the bottom edge. Apps can use the full screen.
dock.behavior.hybrid.desc: Stays on top of maximized apps, which use the full screen. Tap AltGr to hide it, tap again to bring it back.

appearance.syncWindowsAccent.desc: Also use this accent color for Windows itself, like File Explorer highlights and focus borders. Nectar keeps a backup of your current Windows accent and puts it back when you turn this off.
appearance.glassWallpaper.desc: Frosted and Liquid show a blurred copy of your wallpaper behind the notch and dock, and the window behind them when there is one. Off keeps the plain tint. Animated wallpapers are not shown.
notch.hotkey.desc: A global shortcut that hides the notch until you press it again, for example while you click tabs under it. Click the box, then press the keys you want. Clear it to turn the shortcut off.
notch.netWidget.desc: What the Net widget in the collapsed notch shows: live upload and download speed, or an icon for Wi-Fi, Ethernet or offline.
notch.edgeDelay.desc: How long the cursor has to rest on the top edge before the notch opens in Smart and Peek modes. Raise it if it opens while you use tabs or toolbars.
dock.previewDelay.desc: How long the cursor rests on a dock icon before its window preview opens.
dock.hideDelay.desc: How long the dock stays up after the cursor leaves, in Smart and Peek modes.
dock.hybridKey.desc: Hybrid mode only. Tap the key on its own to hide the dock and tap it again to show it. Holding it with another key (like AltGr+Q for @) does nothing. While hidden, the bottom edge does not bring the dock back. It is shown again after a restart.
dock.attention.desc: Mark apps that want your attention, with the unread count when the app shows one

dock.searchShortcut.desc: The shortcut that opens your launcher

dock.searchShortcut.invalid: Use modifiers and one key, like Alt+Space or Ctrl+Shift+K
dock.searchNote.cmdpal: Command Palette isn't running. Turn it on in PowerToys.
dock.searchNote.ptrun: PowerToys Run isn't running. Turn it on in PowerToys.
dock.searchNote.raycast: Couldn't press Raycast's shortcut. Check it in Settings › Dock.

calsync.guide.google.step1: Open Google Calendar on the web (calendar.google.com).
calsync.guide.google.step2: Hover the calendar in the left list, click the three-dot menu, then Settings and sharing.
calsync.guide.google.step3: Scroll to Integrate calendar and copy the Secret address in iCal format.
calsync.guide.google.note: Anyone with this address can read the calendar, so keep it private. Repeat for each calendar you want. If the option is missing, your Google Workspace admin may have turned it off.
calsync.guide.icloud.step1: Open Calendar on icloud.com and sign in.
calsync.guide.icloud.step2: Click the second button from the bottom right of the window.
calsync.guide.icloud.step3: Click the info (i) icon next to the calendar you want.
calsync.guide.icloud.step4: Tick Public Calendar, then copy the link that appears.
calsync.guide.icloud.note: The link starts with webcal://. Paste it as it is. Only that one calendar becomes readable to anyone holding the link, and unticking Public Calendar stops sharing it.
calsync.guide.outlook.step1: In Outlook on the web, open Calendar and click the gear icon for Settings.
calsync.guide.outlook.step2: Go to Calendar, then Shared calendars.
calsync.guide.outlook.step3: Under Publish a calendar, pick the calendar and choose Can view all details.
calsync.guide.outlook.step4: Click Publish. Two links appear: copy the ICS link (it ends in .ics), not the HTML one.
calsync.guide.outlook.note: Work or school accounts often have publishing turned off by an admin. Without Can view all details, events would show without their titles.
calsync.guide.proton.step1: Open Proton Calendar on the web (calendar.proton.me).
calsync.guide.proton.step2: Go to Settings, All settings, Calendars, and choose the calendar.
calsync.guide.proton.step3: Under Share with anyone, click Create link and pick Full view.
calsync.guide.proton.note: Limited view only shows busy blocks with no titles. Anyone with the link can see the calendar, and you can delete the link from its Actions menu to cut off access.
calsync.guide.nextcloud.step1: Open the Calendar app in Nextcloud.
calsync.guide.nextcloud.step2: Click the share icon next to a calendar, then the + next to Share link.
calsync.guide.nextcloud.step3: Copy the link and paste it here. Nectar converts it to the calendar feed for you.
calsync.guide.nextcloud.note: To read your own private calendars without a public link, use the CalDAV account option further down instead.
calsync.guide.other.step1: Find the calendar's iCal or ICS subscription address in its sharing or export settings.
calsync.guide.other.step2: Paste any link that ends in .ics or starts with webcal://.
calsync.guide.other.note: This covers holidays, sports fixtures, school timetables, Fastmail and more. If the link opens a web page instead of downloading a file, it isn't the right one.
calsync.guide.other.label: Other
calsync.account.nextcloud.hint: Create an app password in Nextcloud under Settings › Security › Devices & sessions.
calsync.account.icloud.hint: Apple doesn't allow your real password here. Create an app-specific password at account.apple.com under Sign-In and Security › App-Specific Passwords.
calsync.account.other.hint: Fastmail, Synology, Radicale, Baikal and most other CalDAV servers work. Use an app password if the service offers one.
calsync.account.other.label: Other CalDAV
calsync.links.intro: Paste a link from Google, iCloud, Outlook, Proton and more. No password or sign-in needed, and links are only ever read. They are stored in Windows Credential Manager.
calsync.link.placeholder: Paste a calendar link (https:// or webcal://)
calsync.link.name: Name (optional)
calsync.guide.show: Where do I find my link?
calsync.account.empty: Also reads private calendars. Nextcloud, iCloud and other CalDAV servers.
calsync.account.storage: The password is stored in Windows Credential Manager, never in settings.json.

tour.welcome.title: Welcome to Nectar
tour.welcome.text: This is the notch. Hover it to open it. This tour walks through what you can do with it. Try each step on the real thing, Nectar puts your volume, brightness, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth back when it ends.
tour.panels.title: Scroll to switch panels
tour.panels.text: Scroll the mouse wheel over the notch to switch between music, status, calendar and the Control Center. Try it now.
tour.sliders.title: Sliders
tour.sliders.text: Scroll over the notch to the Control Center or the music panel and drag a volume or brightness slider, or scroll over it to nudge it. Try it now.
tour.controlCenter.title: Control Center
tour.controlCenter.text: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, volume and brightness live here. Click the › on the Wi-Fi tile to see networks, or on Volume to see devices and a slider for each app.
tour.shelf.title: Shelf
tour.shelf.text: Drag a file or text onto the notch to park it on the shelf, then drag it out into any app later. Try dragging one over the notch.
tour.dock.title: The dock
tour.dock.text: In the dock, drag icons to reorder, right-click for options, middle-click for a new window, hover for live previews, or drag a file over an icon to bring that app forward. Try any one.
tour.modes.title: Fixed, Smart or Peek
tour.modes.text: Fixed is always visible, Smart hides when a window covers it, Peek stays hidden until you reach the screen edge. Open the Control Center and click the Notch Mode or Dock Mode tile to try them. Nectar puts it back when the tour ends.
tour.customize.title: Make it yours
tour.customize.text: Themes, notch and dock modes, per-monitor options and a shortcut to hide the notch are in Settings. Prefer the classic look? Turn on Legacy Mode in Settings > General.

notch.timerProgress.desc: Show an edge progress bar on the notch while a timer is active
notch.scrollVolume.desc: Scroll with mouse wheel over the volume and brightness sliders to adjust them
clipboard.empty: Things you copy show up here
notch.panelClipboard.desc: Keep a list of recently copied text, links, images and files in the notch. Items from password managers are skipped
notch.clipboardSize.desc: How many copied items to keep
notch.clipboardPersist.desc: Keep copied text and images after Nectar restarts. They are saved unencrypted on this computer (images as files next to the settings), so leave this off if you copy sensitive content
notch.shelfPersist.desc: Keep files and text on the notch shelf after Nectar restarts. Files are kept as links, not copies. Up to 10 items
notch.rememberMode.desc: When the cursor leaves and comes back, reopen the panel you were on instead of the default panel
notch.hoverOpen.desc: Open a full panel as soon as the cursor is over the notch, instead of only widening it. Switch panels with the icons at the top, the mouse wheel or by clicking the clock
notch.hoverPanel.desc: Which panel the notch opens on. If it is turned off or empty, the notch opens on Status or Music
dock.showDesktop.desc: A thin bar at the right end of the dock, and the bottom-right corner of the screen, show the desktop when clicked (Win+D)
notch.panelControlCenter.desc: Include the Control Center when scrolling through the notch panels
notch.panelShelf.desc: Include the Shelf and accept files and text dropped on the notch
notch.panelOrder.desc: The order the notch panels appear when you scroll through them
notch.ccTiles.desc: Order of the four tiles at the top
overlays.edgeDelay.desc: How long the cursor rests on the screen edge before the slider appears
overlays.side.desc: Screen edge it appears on. The two sliders always use opposite sides
notch.micCam.desc: An orange dot shows while an app uses the microphone and a green dot while one uses the camera. Hover or click the dots in the open notch to see which apps.
notch.micMute.desc: A global shortcut that mutes every microphone for all apps; press it again to unmute. While muted, the notch shows a red microphone, also when closed (yellow if a microphone stays on); click it to unmute. The default is {key} (Win+Alt+K is Windows' own mute for call apps). Clear it to turn meeting mode off.
notch.agentApi.desc: Let AI agents on this computer show their status next to the notch. Applies after a restart
usage.title: Claude usage
notch.claudeUsage.desc: Shows how much of your Claude plan's 5-hour and weekly limits is used and when they reset. The numbers come from Claude Code's status line and the Claude app's own usage history on this PC; your own status line keeps working after Nectar's.
notch.agentStyle.desc: How the notch shows a working agent: a small mascot beside the clock, or a status bar with state and elapsed time
notch.agentSounds.desc: Play a sound when an agent needs input, finishes or fails
dock.clock.desc: Show the time and date at the right end of the dock. Follows the 24-hour setting
dock.network.desc: Show Wi-Fi signal or Ethernet status. Click opens a Wi-Fi and Bluetooth menu
dock.volume.desc: Show the volume level and mute state. Click opens a sound menu with output devices and app volumes
dock.notifications.desc: Show a bell that opens the Windows notification center
dock.media.desc: Show the album art and a play/pause button while something is playing
notch.notifications.desc: Show new Windows notifications as a card in the open notch. Nectar reads them only to show them and never saves their text
notch.notifications.access.denied: Turned off in Windows. Allow apps to access your notifications in Settings > Privacy & security > Notifications
notch.notifications.access.unspecified: Windows hasn't asked yet. Nectar needs access to your notifications to show them
notch.notifications.access.unavailable: This version of Windows doesn't let Nectar read notifications
notch.notifications.hideToasts.desc: Turns off the banner at the bottom right for each app in Windows' own notification settings, so new notifications only show in the notch. They stay in Notification Center. Turning this off, quitting or uninstalling Nectar puts every app's previous setting back. Buttons in a notification (reply, answer a call) only work in Notification Center
notch.notifications.apps.desc: Choose which apps show in the notch. Apps turned off here keep their Windows banners
notch.notifications.apps.empty: No app has sent a notification yet
phone.enable.desc: Send files and text between this PC and your phone and control media, volume and more from it, even on another network. End-to-end encrypted; the PC only makes outbound connections.
phone.clipSync: Send what I copy to my phone
phone.clipSync.desc: Text copied on this PC goes to phones allowed below ("Get the PC clipboard"). Off by default. Text only, up to about 64 KB; what password managers mark private is never sent.
phone.clipSync.noDevice: On, but no phone may get the PC clipboard yet. Allow it here, or tick "Get the PC clipboard" under Phone › Paired phones › Permissions.
phone.clipSync.allSuspended: On, but every paired phone is blocked because its key was used from somewhere else, so none gets the PC clipboard. Remove it under Paired phones and pair again.
phone.state.blocked_proxy: Blocked by the network proxy. The proxy refused the connection; retrying every 5 minutes.
phone.state.blocked_network: No connection to the relay. Retrying…
phone.state.relay_paused: The relay is paused (free Supabase projects pause after a week without use). Resume it in the Supabase dashboard.
phone.state.unclaimed: This PC does not own the relay yet. Finish the one-time owner claim, then retry.
phone.state.anonymousDisabled: Anonymous sign-ins are off on the relay. Turn them on in the Supabase dashboard (Authentication › Sign In / Providers).
phone.pair.desc: Shows a QR code. Scan it with the phone's camera, then type the code the phone shows.
phone.qrHelp: Scan this with your phone's camera. Only scan it where nobody else can see the screen.
phone.request: A phone calling itself "{name}" (name not verified) wants to pair. Type the 6-digit code shown on your phone.
phone.permsAtPairing: What this phone may do (you can change this later):
phone.aborted.second-device: Another device scanned this code. Pairing was cancelled; if you showed the code on a shared screen, start again when only you can see it.
phone.aborted.wrong-code: Three wrong codes. Pairing was cancelled.
phone.aborted.expired: The pairing code expired. Start again.
phone.aborted.relay: The relay refused the pairing. Start again.
phone.suspended: This phone's key was used from somewhere else. Remove it and pair again.
phone.removeConfirm: Remove this phone? It will need to be paired again.
phone.cleanupPending: Removed on this PC, relay cleanup pending. It is retried on every connection.
phone.perm.agentStatus: See Claude status and project names
phone.perm.clipboardOut: Get the PC clipboard (what you copy)
phone.urlRequest: {name} wants to open a link on {host}.
phone.sendFile.desc: Pick a file and send it to this phone (end-to-end encrypted)
phone.sendQueued: The phone is not connected. The file waits for it on the relay for 24 hours.
phone.xfer.state.queued: Waiting for the phone to connect
phone.xfer.err.network: The relay could not be reached
phone.xfer.err.io: Could not read or write the file
phone.xfer.err.timeout: The other side did not answer in time
phone.xfer.err.storage: Not enough space on the phone
phone.xfer.err.folder: The download folder is on a FAT or exFAT drive; pick an NTFS folder
phone.xfer.err.unsupported: The phone's browser cannot receive files
phone.xfer.err.offline: The phone link is not connected
phone.xfer.err.unreadable: The file could not be read
phone.audit.desc: Every pairing, command and transfer is recorded on this PC (never message text). Opens the file's folder.
phone.privacy.desc: Device keys are in Windows Credential Manager for this machine only. Settings export and import never include them.
shelf.sendAllToPhone: Send everything on the shelf to your phone
notch.downloads.desc: Show browser downloads in the notch with bytes and speed, and put finished files on the shelf. Watches the Downloads folder
